Ahluwalia 1 M.Cr.C.No.24 IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH AT JABALPUR BEFORE HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE G. S. AHLUWALIA ON THE 5th OF AUGUST, 2024 MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 24583 of 2023 BRAJESH JHARIYA (MEHRA) AND OTHERS Versus THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Appearance: Shri Chandra Bhushan Tiwari - Advocate for the petitioners. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ORDER
texts.facts: This application under section 482 of CrPC has been filed seeking the following relief:- "It is, therefore, most humbly prayed that the FIR registered against the Petitioners lodged by the respondent no.2, by the police station Gotegoan vide Crime No.0794/2022 for an offences U/S 498-A, 323, 506, 34 IPC and 3,4 Dowry Prohibition Act and Final report, and pending RCT No.1324/2022 deservest to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] in the interest of justice." 2. The applicant no.1 is the husband, applicant no.2 is the mother-in- law, applicant no.3 is the younger brother-in-law (Devar) and applicant no.4 is the spinster sister-in-law (Nanad) of respondent no.2. 3. By this application, the applicants seek quashment of FIR in Crime No.794/2022, registered at Police Station Gotegoan, District Narsinghpur for offence under sections 498-A, 323, 506, 34 of IPC and 3,4 of Dowry Prohibition Act. After reading out the FIR, it is submitted by counsel for the applicants that there is no allegation that the applicants had ever assaulted the respondent no.2. The respondent no.2 had stayed in her matrimonial house only for 6 days i.e 3 days on the first visit and 3 days on the second visit. In fact the applicant no.1 had made a complaint to the police against the Brajesh Jhariya (Mehra) vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80514331/ 1 respondent no.2 and by way of counter-blast, the false FIR has been lodged. Even in the conciliation proceedings, the respondent no.2 had not alleged that she was assaulted or maltreated or treated with cruelty for want of demand of dowry. 4. Per contra, the counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the submissions made by counsel for the applicants. Even before the investigation is completed by the investigating agency, the High Court entertained the writ petition, and by virtue of interim order granted by the High Court, further investigation was stalled.
texts.arguments: The counsel appearing for the appellant also drew our attention to the same decision which is relied upon in the impugned judgment by the High Court i.e. State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal.
